source.title: 40 Student Slots, Real-World Impact — Future of Data Hackathon

core_point: The 2025 Future of Data Hackathon kept its student field to 40, a size picked so every student got direct mentorship and access to executives, while teams spent 12 hours building AI tools for two real Cincinnati nonprofits.
reader_feeling: Students want real experience and career connections, and classes and internships rarely give them the chance to build something a real organization will use while decision-makers watch.
what_we_do: The post told students to register early for one of 40 free slots at the September 6, 2025 hackathon, choose the Beginner Track (Wood Hudson Cancer Research Laboratory) or the Experienced Track (YMCA of Greater Cincinnati), and build an AI solution for that nonprofit's real operational problem, with organizers matching solo registrants into teams.
what_they_get: Per the post: a shot at the $1,000 top prize, unlimited Claude credits via Tembo, a portfolio piece built for and used by a nonprofit, mentor coaching on the Beginner Track, and direct access to corporate executives who came to scout talent.

facts.fact: The 2025 Future of Data Hackathon was set for September 6 (2025) at the 1819 Innovation Hub.
facts.source_quote: The 2025 Future of Data Hackathon runs September 6 at the 1819 Innovation Hub.

facts.fact: The format: twelve hours, two tracks, a $1,000 top prize, unlimited Claude credits, and corporate executives in the room looking for talent.
facts.source_quote: Twelve hours, two tracks, a $1,000 top prize, unlimited Claude credits, and corporate executives in the room looking for talent.
This year, 40 student slots are open

facts.fact: Why 40: small enough that every student gets direct mentorship and meaningful access to the executives in the room, and large enough to form diverse, high-functioning teams.
facts.source_quote: small enough that every student gets direct mentorship and meaningful access to the executives in the room, large enough to form diverse, high-functioning teams.

facts.fact: The Beginner Track partner, Wood Hudson Cancer Research Laboratory, is an independent cancer research institute in Newport, KY, founded in 1981, that maintains over 2 million tissue specimens across breast, colon, gastric, ovarian, and melanoma research lines.
facts.source_quote: a 1981-founded independent cancer research institute in Newport, KY that maintains over 2 million tissue specimens across breast, colon, gastric, ovarian, and melanoma research lines.

facts.fact: On the Experienced Track, teams worked with the YMCA of Greater Cincinnati on advanced AI for community programs.
facts.source_quote: Experienced Track: teams collaborate with the YMCA of Greater Cincinnati on advanced AI for community programs.

facts.fact: Movers & Makers covered the partnership when registration opened, reporting that both nonprofits submitted real operational problems for the teams to solve.
facts.source_quote: Movers & Makers covered the partnership when registration opened: both nonprofits submitted real operational problems for the teams to solve.
facts.attribution: Movers & Makers (Cincinnati local press), per the post

facts.fact: At the 2024 hackathon (which the post calls last year), a team walked in with nothing but curiosity and a caffeine plan. By dusk they had shipped a working prototype, won thousands of dollars, and gained a new belief in what was possible.
facts.source_quote: Last year, a team walked in with nothing but curiosity and a caffeine plan. By dusk, they'd shipped a working prototype, won thousands of dollars, and gained a new belief in what was possible.
facts.attribution: Future of Data Hackathon Team, per the post

facts.fact: The unlimited Claude credits came from Tembo, the hackathon's AI tooling partner.
facts.source_quote: The Unlimited Claude credits come via Tembo, the hackathon's AI tooling partner.

facts.fact: The executives in the room are decision-makers who come to see who builds well under pressure.
facts.source_quote: The executives in the room are decision-makers who show up to see who builds well under pressure.

facts.fact: The post says a strong showing at the hackathon has historically led to internship offers, job referrals, and mentorship relationships that last well past event day.
facts.source_quote: A strong showing at the hackathon has historically translated into internship offers, job referrals, and mentorship relationships that extend well past event day.

facts.fact: The event was free to attend.
facts.source_quote: The event is free to attend.

opener.why: The post's most vivid moment is a surprising result: a 2024 team that arrived with nothing but curiosity and a caffeine plan had a working prototype by dusk (F8). That leads naturally into the 2025 event's model of a small cohort building for real nonprofits.

linkedin_angle: The reader should see that the Future of Data Hackathon was built around outcomes: a deliberately small 40-student cohort, real problems from Wood Hudson Cancer Research Laboratory and the YMCA of Greater Cincinnati, and executives in the room to see who builds well under pressure.
instagram_hook_idea: Lead with the 2024 team that walked in with nothing but curiosity and a caffeine plan and had a working prototype by dusk.
cautions: PAST EVENT: the hackathon was September 6, 2025 and the post was published 2025-08-30. Today is 2026-10-16. Describe only what the post says was planned or offered, in past tense. Never state attendance, results, winners, or outcomes of the 2025 event, which the post could not know when it was written. No call to action that has expired: no 'register now', no 'slots fill first come', no DevPost registration push.
The title has an em dash ('40 Student Slots, Real-World Impact — Future of Data Hackathon'). Rewrite it, never quote it.

Rob Richardson's closing quote has an em dash ('This is where builders become leaders — by building for people first.'), so it is left out of the facts. Do not quote it. Many other body sentences use em dashes too. The verified source_quotes avoid them; do not pull in other sentences.

F8 is credited to the 'Future of Data Hackathon Team' and is about the 2024 event. Keep that attribution and that year. 'Thousands of dollars' is the post's vague phrasing: do not turn it into a specific amount or combine it with the 2025 $1,000 prize.
F11 is hedged with 'historically'. Keep the hedge, and do not promise that participants got jobs or internships.
F5 says 'over 2 million' tissue specimens. Keep 'over'. Wood Hudson does cancer research, so keep the tone respectful and do not suggest that student tools cured, diagnosed, or treated anyone.
F7 is third-party press. Credit it to Movers & Makers.

The post uses 'not X, Y' contrasts that the Writer must not copy: 'a 12-hour sprint, not an open-enrollment course', 'designed to be used, not archived', 'applied access to a production AI tool, not a classroom simulation'.
'First come, first built' is the post's own registration wordplay and belongs to an expired call to action. It is not a listed DN canon framework.
The post says DN/MidwestCon convenes the event (see first_party). Write it as our own event, but still in past tense.
visual_note: Use a real photo of students building at the 1819 Innovation Hub or of the hackathon itself, not an AI-generated image. If a logo is used: white lockup on dark backgrounds, dark lockup on light, purple 'Now' unchanged, no effects.

key_dates: 2024 (the previous hackathon, which the post calls last year)
timeframe.handling: Describe only what the post says was planned or offered, in past tense. Never state attendance, results, or outcomes the post could not know when it was written. No call to action that has expired (registration, slot availability, DevPost sign-up).

first_party.what: The 2025 Future of Data Hackathon, which runs under MidwestCon. The byline bio says Rob Richardson founded and convenes MidwestCon.
